newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent stalled, but seen supported on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent stalled, but seen supported on Iraq.

text.p: Brent crude futures were untraded and stalled at midday on Thursday, waiting for further direction from London.
July was offered at $20.20 per barrel. No bid was seen. Other contracts were unquoted.
In London overnight, the July contract rose 13 cents per barrel to $20.13, pushed by a firmer tone on NYMEX.
July NYMEX crude, trading on the after-hours ACCESS system in Asia, was last traded at $21.82 per barrel, down four cents from New York in moderate volume of 382 lots.

Brokers said they expected the market to remain supported by news of Turkish incursions into Northern Iraq, which is unnerving neighbours. Turkey's state-run news agency Anatolian said Syria, Iraq and Iran were building up forces on the borders of the Kurdish safe-haven in northern Iraq.
Technically, brokers said they expected July Brent to be supported at $20.00, a 50-percent retracement of last Friday's rally.
